explanation: Agoh's formulation: n ≥ 2 is prime iff n·B_{n−1} ≡ −1 (mod n). This is encoded as n² | n·num + den with B = num/den in lowest terms. I checked that this matches the intended congruence. If n | den (which happens exactly when n is squarefree with (q−1) | (n−1) for all q | n, by von Staudt–Clausen), then n·B + 1 = (num + den/n)/(den/n), so the congruence holds iff n | num + den/n, equivalent to the encoding. If n ∤ den, both fail. For n = 2, using bernoulli' (B₁ = +1/2) gives 2·½ = 1 ≡ −1 mod 2, as required. The statement is faithful and open.
